The platform is browser-only, with no app to install. Signals arrive from the models, trades execute through a broker partner, and the US$250 minimum opens access to 8 assets and the demo.
We do not trade on the platforms we review and we take no referral position in the verdict. We read the pages, verify what is verifiable, and score what remains.
whatItClaims: Free registration, with account activation by confirmation link.
Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
No prior trading experience required.
whatWeChecked: The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.
The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.
The security claims: encryption and account protection statements.
The withdrawal path: steps and any fees the page omits.
The ownership trail: who operates the platform and where.
The support channels: live chat, email or phone availability.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Create the account with your contact details, then verify it through the emailed link.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Add US$250 to the account through the payment options shown at checkout.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Set your risk settings, choose automatic or manual mode, and keep the demo running while you learn.

pros: Fast setup - minutes to a live dashboard.
cons: Performance examples without dates or proof.
Asset list that shifts between pages.
The headline fee claim and the real cost disagree.
redFlags: Restriction lists that name different countries.
Payout promises with no processing detail.
No regulator, licence or audit named anywhere.

faqs.a: The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$250 minimum.
The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$250 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.
US$250, funded by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill. It is trading capital in your balance, not a fee - and it is exposed to market risk once live.

bottomLine: For a cautious newcomer, Romalizio IA can work: start on the demo, deposit the US$250 minimum and keep your own numbers.
The final score lands at 4.7 - a capable platform held back by its own paperwork. Start small, verify the claims yourself and never trade money you cannot lose.
